# 1. Data layer: what the agent sees

[← Home](../README.md) · [The stack](README.md) · **Data layer** · [Agent layer](agent.md) · [Execution layer](execution.md) · [Harness layer](harness.md) · [Application layer](application.md)

> **What did the agent know, and when did it know it?**

**Scope.** Market, fundamental, filing and news data; connectors that hand data to an agent (MCP servers); datasets; and the step that turns text into signals.

**Where it usually breaks:** restated fundamentals overwriting the originals; news timestamps that are crawl times, not publication times; survivorship in the universe; adjusted prices that embed later splits; prompt injection through news text.

**Open gap.** Almost no agent framework ships a point-in-time store. The MCP data servers listed here serve current data; none was checked for point-in-time guarantees, so none should feed a backtest unaudited.

Legend: 🟢 active · 🟡 slowing · ⚪ dormant (last commit within 90 days, within a year, or older, counted from the check date) · 💤 declared unmaintained · ⚡ can place real orders · 📝 paper trading only · 🧩 open core with proprietary parts · 🔒 source-available, restricted · ❓ license unclear · 🧰 general-purpose tool applied here · 📖 read in full · 🗂️ machine-extracted [method card](../docs/cards/index.md) · 🔖 abstract only. ## Also relevant from other layers

Listed in their primary layer; they also ship working code for this one.

- [Alpaca MCP Server](https://github.com/alpacahq/alpaca-mcp-server) — MCP server letting LLM clients query market data and place Alpaca orders. *Primary: [Execution layer](execution.md).*
- [FinGPT](https://github.com/AI4Finance-Foundation/FinGPT) — Open financial LLM project with data pipelines and LoRA fine-tuning recipes. *Primary: [Agent layer](agent.md).*
- [FinRobot](https://github.com/AI4Finance-Foundation/FinRobot) — Equity-research agent platform where code computes figures and LLMs write narrative. *Primary: [Application layer](application.md).*
- [Qlib](https://github.com/microsoft/qlib) — Quant research platform with data layer, ML model zoo and backtest tooling. *Primary: [Harness layer](harness.md).*

## Articles and posts

Newest first. Icons: 𝕏 post · 📝 blog · 📘 docs · 📰 news · 🎧 podcast · 🎤 talk · 📄 paper or report. A post is listed for the idea it carries; its own performance claims are not verified here. Undated pages show the date we checked them.

- 📘 [TradingView MCP Server: setup and tool reference](https://www.tradingview.com/mcp/docs) — TradingView, undated (checked 2026-10-26). Official hosted MCP server (beta, 35 tools: watchlists, OHLCV, screener, technicals, news, fundamentals, alerts). It has no order tools, and its write tools only change watchlists and alerts.
- 📘 [TradingView MCP Server FAQ](https://www.tradingview.com/support/solutions/43000795700-mcp-server-faq/) — TradingView, undated (checked 2026-10-26). Read before wiring it into an agent: data is delayed even with a real-time subscription, Pine and indicator alerts are not in the beta, and unattended or server-hosted use is out of scope. It suits interactive research, not an unattended data feed.
- 🔧 [NAAIM Exposure Index](https://naaim.org/programs/naaim-exposure-index/) — National Association of Active Investment Managers, undated (checked 2026-10-26). Primary source for a widely quoted positioning gauge. Public data carries a three-month delay, so a current reading quoted in a post usually cannot be checked from here.
- 📘 [sqzme monitor documentation (DIX and GEX)](https://squeezemetrics.com/monitor/docs) — SqueezeMetrics, undated (checked 2026-10-26). Primary definitions of dark-pool (DIX) and gamma-exposure (GEX) measures, with the vendor's own stated limitations. Check thresholds attributed to the vendor against this page.
- 𝕏 [A five-group checklist for judging a selloff: VIX term structure, put/call, dealer gamma, short interest, flows and sentiment](https://x.com/youngstockuser/status/2114326634547311060) — @youngstockuser, 2026-10-25. A practitioner's map of where each risk gauge comes from and how it is read, in Chinese. Useful as a data-source checklist; it is a viewpoint, not a tested bottom signal, and one threshold it attributes to a vendor is not in the vendor's docs.
- 📝 [Advancing Claude for Financial Services](https://www.anthropic.com/news/advancing-claude-for-financial-services) — Anthropic, 2025-10-27. Market-data connectors (LSEG, Moody's, Aiera, MT Newswires and others) and finance Agent Skills: a concrete example of packaging data access and analyst workflows as skills.

## Builder notes

Recommendations from this list's maintainers, distilled from the sources above. They are design advice, not results reported by those sources.

- **Keep an evidence record, not just a value.** Store every fetched fact with its source URL, `published_at`, `retrieved_at` and a label: fact, inference, hypothesis or unknown. A citation that matches the source text shows the source says it; it does not show the inference drawn from it.
- **Show conflicting indicators instead of voting.** When combining risk gauges (VIX, put/call, dealer gamma, short interest, flows, sentiment), split them by index, sector and holding, show the ones that disagree with their source and as-of time, and do not add them up into a single score.
- **Session and pivot features must not peek.** Chart features such as session high/low (killzones) and swing-anchored VWAP are event features, not signals. Define sessions in exchange time with daylight saving (for US futures, America/New_York), use only reference levels visible at that moment, define break and reclaim exactly, and confirm a pivot only after its right-hand bars have closed.
- **An installed connector is not a working feed.** A connector that installs and passes its health check has not yet returned correct data. Pin versions, whitelist read-only tools, keep the raw response and its timestamp, and compare price, time, gaps and latency against a licensed source before trusting it.
